title: KV cache fragmentation reduction and allocation strategy for continuous batching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: As continuous batching increases throughput, the per-request KV cache allocations on the GPU exhibit fragmentation over long-running worker lifetimes. Fragmentation causes higher peak memory usage, occasional OOMs under load spikes, and suboptimal packing of hot KV entries. Goal: design and implement a KV cache allocation and compaction strategy that reduces internal fragmentation, maintains low tail latency for small batches, and preserves the benefits of prefix/KV reuse for cost efficiency. Scope includes allocator policy, in-place compaction heuristics, eviction/aging integration, and metrics for fragmentation detection.
implementation_notes: Use a hybrid allocator: fixed-size power-of-two slab classes for small KV entries, and a pooled large-block allocator for big sequences to avoid internal fragmentation.
Track allocation churn per slab class and per worker to trigger background compaction when fragmentation ratio > 25% for N consecutive minutes.
Implement lazy compaction combined with short-stop-the-world defragmentation windows scheduled during low-util periods (predict via request rate), keeping stop durations < 5ms where possible.
Introduce per-model and per-sequence aging counters so the eviction policy prefers evicting cold prefix slices while preserving recent KV cache hits used by continuous batching.

Expose new metrics: fragmentation_ratio, slab_usage_by_class, compaction_time_ms, compaction_pause_ms, kv_evictions_due_to_frag, peak_reserved_gpu_mem. Instrument both per-pod and cluster aggregated views.
Make compaction opt-in via runtime config flag; default policy will be conservative on Dedicated until e2e safety checks pass.
Implement a simulation harness that replays production KV allocation traces (from continuous batching workloads) to validate allocator behavior before rollout.
Correlation with batch size distributions: prefer coalescing small adjacent KV allocations created by the same request stream to reduce holes when those requests complete together.
Consider GPU memory allocator integration points (CUDA IPC/malloc hooks or internal memory manager) to minimize cross-layer synchronization overhead.
Ensure compatibility with current quantization/kernel selection paths and that compaction does not change KV pointer stability expected by the runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic replay: reduce fragmentation_ratio by >= 40% on representative production traces compared to baseline
Observed peak GPU reserved memory reduced by >= 15% in long-running worker experiments without increasing 95th percentile latency by more than 5%
No regression OOMs on the dedicated cluster during 48-hour soak with continuous batching workload
New metrics present in console dashboards and alerts configured for fragmentation_ratio > 30%
Design doc and code reviews approved; at least one canary rollout on a non-critical fleet with monitoring dashboards green for 24 hours
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests; 2) Replay harness validation off-line against last 30 days of allocation traces; 3) Merge behind runtime feature flag; 4) Canary on 5% of Dedicated nodes for 24h with observability; 5) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% after 72h green; 6) Enable on Hosted with additional telemetry and opt-out for heavy-tail customers if needed.
regression_risks: Short stop-the-world compaction could increase p99 latency if scheduled poorly; allocator bugs could cause pointer invalidation leading to correctness issues. Mitigations: conservative defaults, pointer-stability invariants, extensive unit + integration tests, and canary rollout.
